rfi.title: EU vows to defend climate science as Cop31 talks expose global divisions

rfi.title: France marks 11th anniversary of Paris attacks with tribute at Stade de France
rfi.description: France is marking the 11th anniversary of the November 2015 Paris terrorist attacks on Friday, with commemorations honouring the 130 people killed. This year the Stade de France, one of the sites targeted by the attackers, hosts a sporting event on 13 November for the first time since the tragedy.

rfi.title: Ukraine peace talks overshadow AI summit as EU leaders gather in Dublin
rfi.description: European Union leaders are gathering in Dublin on Friday for a summit dominated by efforts to secure Europe's place in negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, while also confronting the growing challenge of artificial intelligence and the bloc's ability to compete with the United States and China in the sector.

rfi.title: France slams Russian ‘intimidation’ as fresh EU sanctions come into force
rfi.description: The European Union will approve more ​sanctions against Russia on Monday, the bulk of which were proposed by France, the country's Minister for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad said on Thursday. He also warned that Paris would not be intimidated by Moscow’s decision to ban two French journalists and two MPs from entering the country.

rfi.title: German chemical sector enraged by Merz's backing of EU carbon scheme
rfi.description: Germany’s chemical industry has sharply criticised Chancellor Friedrich Merz after he reportedly urged the European Commission to press ahead with the European Union’s expanded carbon-pricing scheme, calling the plan in its current form the “gravedigger” of European industry.

rfi.title: Amnesty demands answers over failure to prevent South Sudan massacre
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused South Sudanese authorities and UN peacekeepers of failing to prevent a massacre earlier this year, despite advance warnings of an imminent attack.

rfi.title: Global Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook and other services
rfi.description: Microsoft’s Outlook email service has been down since late on Thursday, disrupting businesses and government agencies in 74 countries and territories. On Friday the company said the outage was caused by a heavy load on its infrastructure, rather than by malicious activity.

rfi.title: Algerian writer Kamel Daoud sentenced to five years over prize-winning novel
rfi.description: Franco-Algerian writer Kamel Daoud and his wife have each been sentenced to five years in prison by an Algerian court over allegations that his award-winning novel Houris drew on confidential medical information about a woman who survived an Islamist attack during the country's civil war in the 1990s.

rfi.title: Migration to wealthy countries slows for second year amid tougher rules
rfi.description: Legal migration to developed countries dropped for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, as governments tightened rules for workers, students and refugees, according to an OECD report published Thursday. But the figures show sharply diverging trends – with big increases in Southern Europe and sharp declines in North America.

rfi.title: Medical charity warns funding for DRC Ebola fight not reaching front lines
rfi.description: Six months into the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, the virus is continuing to spread and international aid is not reaching the front line, French medical charity Doctors Without Borders said on ‌Thursday.

rfi.title: African push to triple climate adaptation finance left off Cop31 agenda
rfi.description: African countries’ proposal to triple finance for adaptation to the effects of climate change has been left off the agenda at the United Nations climate summit Cop31, currently under way in Antalya, Turkey. Wealthy nations pushed back against efforts to make it a formal, binding agenda item.

rfi.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom as first black senator since 19th century

rfi.title: France's Macron to pay state visit to Cambodia during Francophonie summit

It will be the first visit by a French president to Cambodia since Charles de Gaulle’s in 1966.

lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, « L’Epoque » paie son coup. Depuis les hauteurs de Montmartre, l’autrice-compositrice-interprète raconte sa quête de précision des mots et des sons. Elle sera sur la scène de la Salle Pleyel, le 3 décembre.

france24fr.title: Rugby : les Bleus signent un succès majeur face aux Springboks
france24fr.description: Le XV de France a remporté une victoire majuscule, la plus marquante depuis le Mondial 2023, en battant les doubles champions du monde sud-africains vendredi au Stade de France (21-19). Malgré de nombreuses blessures, l'équipe de France a su rivaliser, en conservant jusqu'au bout l'avance acquise lors d'une première mi-temps flamboyante.

france24fr.title: Panne mondiale chez Microsoft : l'Europe sous dépendance ?
france24fr.description: La panne de Microsoft illustre une nouvelle fois la vulnérabilité européenne. Comment mettre fin à la dépendance? On en parle avec Martin Hullin de la Fondation Bertelsmann.

france24fr.title: Ballaké Sissoko : un nouvel album pour son père, la mémoire du Mali au son de la kora
france24fr.description:
Le virtuose malien de la kora Ballaké Sissoko revient avec Djelimady N°1, un nouvel album attendu le 27 novembre 2026. Un disque profondément personnel, dédié à son père Djelimady Sissoko, figure majeure de la musique mandingue et membre fondateur de l'Ensemble instrumental national du Mali.

De son enfance à Bamako à ses rencontres avec de grands musiciens internationaux, Ballaké Sissoko raconte son parcours, son attachement à la kora et son désir de transmettre un patrimoine musical exceptionn

france24fr.title: JOJ de Dakar, clap de fin : succès et satisfaction pour une première en Afrique
france24fr.description: Clap de fin aux 4e Jeux Olympique de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026. Après deux semaines de compétition 5 pays africains se sont classés dans le top 10 du classement des médailles à savoir l'Egypte, l'Ethiopie, le Senegal, le Kenya et l'Afrique du Sud, une première dans l'histoire des jeux. Les athlètes et encadreurs ont manifesté leur entière satisfaction sur l'organisation de ce premier évènement olympique en Afrique.

france24fr.title: Mort de Jesus de Miguel : l'équato-guinéen Jesus Owono fixé sur son sort
france24fr.description: La Fédération espagnole de football a opté pour la plus lourde sanction à sa disposition. Le gardien de but d'Andorre Jesus Owono est suspendu 12 matches pour avoir percuté Jesus de Miguel, décédé le lendemain des suites du choc.

france24fr.title: "Rasez cette maison" : comment les internautes ont guidé un raid anti-gang de Bukele en Haïti
france24fr.description: Le président salvadorien Nayib Bukele a annoncé la destruction du quartier général des "400 Mawozo", l’un des principaux gangs haïtiens. L'opération militaire semble avoir été déclenchée à la suite d'un échange sur X, et aidé par les talents de géolocalisation d'un expert de l'OSINT. Dans la foulée, une image virale a prétendu montrer l'arrestation du chef de ce gang "Lanmò San Jou", alias Wilson Joseph. En réalité, elle était manipulée par l'IA sur la base d'une photo prise il y a deux ans.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : l'agence de l'aviation civile ordonne l'arrêt de tous les vols à cause d'un problème de communication
États-Unis : les vols arrêtés dans les aéroports du pays en raison d'un problème de communication
france24fr.description: L'Administration fédérale de l’aviation (FAA) a annoncé vendredi que les vols dans l'ensemble des aéroports américains sont mis à l'arrêt en raison d’un problème de communication affectant tous les centres de contrôle du trafic aérien, a déclaré le secrétaire américain aux Transports Sean Duffy.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : le Mali arrache la victoire au Rwanda et prend déjà une option
france24fr.description: Le Mali a battu le Rwanda 3 à 2, vendredi, à Bamako, lors de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Une victoire qui place les Aigles en tête du groupe K et dans un fauteuil pour se qualifier pour la Coupe d'Afrique.

france24fr.title: Affaire Nvidia, guerre en Ukraine, tractations en Israël et sort de Christophe Gleizes
france24fr.description: Au sommaire de l'émission cette semaine: la démission du PDG de Nvidia Jensen Huang, après la révélation d'une relation extra-conjuguale avec une femme soupçonnée d'être une espionne chinoise; la reprise des discussions autour de la guerre en Ukraine à Abou Dhabi, une première en 8 mois; la première session houleuse de la nouvelle Knesset en Israël; et l'appel de la famille de Christophe Gleizes à la libération du journaliste, emprisonné en Algérie depuis plus de 500 jours.

france24fr.title: Jacques Nesi :" les soldats salvadoriens sotn accueillis comme le Messie en Haïti"
france24fr.description: Depuis fin octobre, quelques 2000 soldats salvadoriens sont déployés en Haïti, en accord avec l'exécutif haïtien. Ces militaires ont été initialement envoyés pour retrouver quatre soldats salvadoriens membres de la force onusienne, portés disparus après une attaque de gangs. Mais la durée et l'ampleur de l'opération menée par le Salvador interroge sur les réelles intentions du président Nayib Bukele. Jacques Nesi, politologue à l’Université des Antilles, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : les Européens seront représentés par cinq pays, dont la France, aux négociations sur l'Ukraine
Projet de loi résilience : comment la France veut rattraper son retard en cybersécurité
france24fr.description: Alors que les cyberattaques se multiplient en France, l’Assemblée s'apprête à adopter, mardi, la loi résilience sur le renforcement de la cybersécurité. Retardé depuis deux ans, le texte multiplie par dix le nombre d’entités régulées et impose des sanctions financières en cas de manquement aux obligations de prévention, sans prévoir de financements supplémentaires.

france24fr.title: Urgence climatique : la rente pétrolière difficile à lâcher ?
france24fr.description: Alors que l’urgence climatique s’aggrave, la mobilisation politique s’essouffle. Ouverte ce lundi à Antalya, en Turquie, la COP31 se déroule dans une indifférence quasi générale. L’absence de nombreux dirigeants, les divisions persistantes et l’opposition de l’Amérique de Donald Trump à l’action climatique freinent les ambitions.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : le Nigeria se relance, la Tunisie chute et se met en danger
france24fr.description: La troisième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 continue. Le Nigeria s'est imposé à domicile face à la Tanzanie (3-1) tandis que la Tunisie s'est inclinée contre la Libye (0-2).

france24fr.title: Un radar américain détruit par l'Iran ? Cette image modifiée par IA montre une destruction ancienne
france24fr.description: Le 13 novembre, l'Iran a affirmé avoir détruit un radar américain à Bahreïn, ce que les États-Unis démentent. Une image satellite modifiée par IA, censée prouver l'attaque iranienne, a ensuite circulé en ligne. Elle avait été publiée dès juin, après de précédentes attaques iraniennes qui avaient bien endommagé un site américain.

france24fr.title: "Ils nous ont tués" : Novaïa Gazeta ferme, la presse libre disparaît en Russie
france24fr.description: Lundi 9 novembre, les journalistes de Novaïa Gazeta, dernier journal indépendant de Russie, ont été contraints de quitter les locaux historiques de leur rédaction à Moscou. Sous pression constante, le média a été déclaré "agent de l'étranger". L'un de ses collaborateurs, Oleg Roldouguine, qui enquêtait sur la corruption des élites, est accusé d'avoir "divulgué des données personnelles en rédigeant des articles négatifs sur les Russes". Une intense émotion a accompagné cette fermeture.

france24fr.title: Non, des femmes palestiniennes n’ont pas agressé une journaliste européenne
france24fr.description: Le 11 novembre sur X, un utilisateur pro-israélien a instrumentalisé une vidéo pour dénoncer la supposée violence de femmes palestiniennes envers une journaliste européenne. La vidéo est en réalité issue d’un reportage en Syrie datant de 2024. La publication, devenue virale, a rapidement été corrigée par d’autres internautes.

zeit.title: Gipfel in China: Weißes Haus kündigt Dreiertreffen Trumps mit Xi und Putin an
Bundeshaushalt: Bundesrechnungshof mahnt Union und SPD zu härterem Sparkurs
zeit.description: Ansgar Heveling drängt auf eine wirksame Schuldenregel. Der Chef des Bundesrechnungshofs kritisiert, Deutschland lebe »offenkundig über seine Verhältnisse«.

zeit.title: Luftverkehr: Europäische Flugbehörde: Derzeit keine Flüge in die USA
Luftverkehr: Europäische Flugbehörde: Derzeit keine Flüge in die USA
Regierungsbildung in Berlin: Linke-Chef verteidigt langwieriges Verfahren zu Vanessa Emde
Regel gilt seit einem Monat: Alkoholverbot an Bahnhöfen: Bahn zieht positive Bilanz
Luftverkehr in den USA: US-Luftfahrtbehörde ordnet Startverbot an allen Flughäfen an
zeit.description: Die US-Luftfahrtaufsicht hat einen landesweiten Stopp für Starts an Flughäfen verfügt. Es gebe gravierende Kommunikationsprobleme, meldete der Verkehrsminister.

zeit.title: Luftverkehr in den USA: US-Luftfahrtbehörde ordnet Startverbot an allen Flughäfen an
zeit.description: Die US-Luftfahrtaufsicht hat einen landesweiten Stopp für Starts an Flughäfen verfügt. Es gebe gravierende Kommunikationsprobleme, meldete der Verkehrsminister.

zeit.title: RAF Lakenheath: US-Luftwaffe meldet Vorfall mit Drohnen an Stützpunkt in England
zeit.description: An einem britischen Stützpunkt ist es laut dem US-Militär zu »unbefugten Drohnenaktivitäten« gekommen. Personal und Infrastruktur seien nicht beeinträchtigt worden.

zeit.title: Kreuzfahrtschiff gekentert: Keine Vermissten nach Schiffsunglück in New Orleans
CDU: Ex-Bundesverkehrsminister: Hege keinen Groll gegen Merz
USA: Tanker und Flusskreuzfahrtschiff kollidieren in New Orleans
zeit.description: In Louisiana sind zwei Schiffe zusammengestoßen. Eines hatte über 120 Menschen an Bord. Auf Aufnahmen war zu sehen, wie eines der Schiffe sinkt.

zeit.title: Störung bei Microsoft: Microsoft führt Störung auf Netzwerkupgrade zurück
zeit.description: Ein internes Problem hat die stundenlange Störung der Dienste verursacht, teilt Microsoft mit. Eine Cyberattacke oder KI-Aktivitäten schließt der Konzern aus.

zeit.title: Nations League, 5. Spieltag: Deutschland schlägt Serbien
zeit.description: Deutschland besiegt Serbien in der Nations League. Die DFB-Elf geht früh durch ein Eigentor in Führung, nach zwei Roten Karten spielt sie in Überzahl. Der Spielbericht

nzz.title: «Aussergewöhnliche Umstände»: USA verhängen landesweites Startverbot
nzz.description: Aufgrund einer technischen Panne in den Kontrollzentren hat die US-Luftfahrtbehörde FAA am Freitag sämtliche Abflüge in den Vereinigten Staaten bis auf weiteres gestoppt.

nzz.title: Wird das Starship nun komplett wiederverwendbar? SpaceX bricht das Auffangen der unteren Raketenstufe ab, die obere Raketenstufe erreicht das All
nzz.description: Derzeit findet der nächste Testflug der Rakete von Elon Musks Raumfahrtfirma statt. Läuft der Flug gut, ist das ein echter Durchbruch für die Raumfahrt.

nzz.title: Die Schweizer Fussballer sichern sich dank dem torlosen Remis in Slowenien den Gruppensieg in der Nations League
nzz.description: Das Schweizer Nationalteam schafft den schnellstmöglichen Wiederaufstieg in die Liga A. Das Auswärtsspiel in Maribor wird aber niemand lange in Erinnerung behalten.

nzz.title: Tankschiff rammt Kreuzfahrtschiff auf dem Mississippi in New Orleans
nzz.description: Ein Tanker ist am Freitag auf dem Mississippi mit einem vertäuten Flusskreuzfahrtschiff kollidiert. TV-Aufnahmen zeigten Passagiere in Rettungswesten im Wasser, mindestens 14 Personen wurden gerettet.

nzz.title: Deutschland gewinnt sicher gegen Serbien
nzz.description: Schon nach einer Viertelstunde führten die Gäste durch ein Eigentor und einen Treffer von Florian Wirtz mit 2:0.

nzz.title: Die US-Demokraten gewinnen überraschend auch im konservativen Mississippi – die Resultate der Midterms im Überblick
nzz.description: Seit der Wahlnacht ist klar, dass die Demokraten in beiden Kammern des amerikanischen Kongresses die Macht übernehmen. Aber mit fortschreitender Auszählung nehmen ihre Sitzgewinne noch zu.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Massive Störung bei Microsoft geht auf Netzwerk-Upgrade zurück: die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten
nzz.description: Eine Störung bei Microsoft hat in 74 Ländern etliche Dienste des Softwarekonzerns lahmgelegt. Viele Unternehmen und Verbraucher meldeten auch noch am Freitag Probleme bei E-Mails.

nzz.title: Alle gegen alle: Nach dem Absturz des Budgets schieben sich die Parteien gegenseitig die Schuld zu
nzz.description: Am Mittwoch lehnte die Finanzkommission überraschend den Haushalt für das kommende Jahr ab. Noch ist unklar, was das für Auswirkungen hat.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: EU einig: Verhandlungsteam für Gespräche mit Russland steht +++ Putin laut Kushner bereit für Europäer am Verhandlungstisch
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Frontex meldet 29 Prozent weniger irreguläre Grenzübertritte
nzz.description: Über die griechischen Inseln, die Balkanroute oder den Ärmelkanal versuchen noch immer täglich Migranten, unter Lebensgefahr nach Europa zu gelangen.

nzz.title: Die SVP und der Ticket-Poker: Aussenseiter im Bundesratsrennen hoffen auf einen Dreiervorschlag
nzz.description: Thomas Aeschi gilt bei der SVP-Leitung als Favorit für die Nachfolge von Bundesrat Guy Parmelin. Die Wahlchancen des Zugers hängen auch von der Grösse des Tickets ab.

nzz.title: Kann sich Mercedes Deutschland noch leisten? Darum eskaliert jetzt der Konflikt bei dem Autohersteller
nzz.description: Das Management des Stuttgarter Konzerns ringt mit der Gewerkschaft erbittert um Privilegien wie die 35-Stunden-Woche. Der Streit wird zum Testfall für die gesamte deutsche Autobranche.

nzz.title: Für Daniel Grieder wurde es bei Hugo Boss ungemütlich – nun endet sein Abenteuer dort früher als geplant
nzz.description: Der Schweizer Manager hat den Modekonzern verjüngt, aber bei den Anlegern ist die Euphorie über seine ambitionierten Pläne verflogen. Das liess ihn auch der neue Besitzer spüren.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - SP und SVP blockieren das Bundesbudget: Sie gefährden damit das Schweizer Erfolgsmodell und zeigen, dass sie das Volk offenbar für sehr naiv halten
nzz.description: Nach aussen geben sich die Polparteien als standfeste Volksvertreter, doch ihre Taktik der Profilierung ist in erster Linie ein Täuschungsmanöver – das schadet nicht nur der Schweiz, sondern möglicherweise auch den Interessen der Parteien.

nzz.title: Der Nachweis von K.-o.-Tropfen scheitert oft am schnellen Abbau des Stoffs im Körper. Ein neuer Biomarker könnte das bald ändern
nzz.description: Zürcher Rechtsmediziner sind einem Abbauprodukt des Betäubungsmittels GHB auf der Spur, das länger nachweisbar ist als der Stoff selbst. Eine Studie macht nun Hoffnung, dass Täter in Zukunft öfter überführt werden können.

nzz.title: Die neue Parkkarte wird für die Stadt Zürich zu einem juristischen Albtraum: Jetzt wird sie gleich durch zwei Rechtsverfahren blockiert
nzz.description: Bürgerliche in der Stadt Zürich fühlen sich von Rot-Grün wegen der Parkkarte verschaukelt – nun blockieren sie diese mit Rechtsmitteln.

observador.title: UE vai enviar seis representantes para negociar com a Rússia
observador.description: Esta foi a solução encontrada após não ter sido possível encontrar um nome único para representar o bloco europeu nas negociações. Costa, Kallas e Stubb eram os nomes mais falados.

observador.title: Sindicato dos Jornalistas leva patrões ao Ministério
observador.description: A tabela salarial do CCT da Imprensa, aprovada em 2023, ficará "fora da lei" em 2026, quando o salário mínimo sobe para 970 euros e supera dois escalões do contrato.

observador.title: Cais palafítico da Lagoa de Óbidos em risco após colapso
observador.description: Construído em 2023 na Lagoa de Óbidos, o cais está interditado desde agosto. A Câmara das Caldas da Rainha ainda aguarda parecer da Universidade do Minho.

observador.title: Detidos quatro espanhóis em lancha rápida nas Berlengas
observador.description: 13 elementos da Polícia Marítima intercetaram a embarcação numa zona da reserva natural. Outras três embarcações fugiram ao detetar as autoridades.

observador.title: Alemanha autoriza serviços secretos a realizar sabotagens
observador.description: Nova lei permite a realização de operações clandestinas, no quadro do aumento da ameaça russa. Ministro do Interior defende medida para combeter "os inimigos da democracia, dentro e fora do país".

observador.title: Atraso do ministério deixa orquestra sem metade dos docentes
observador.description: Dois meses após o início das aulas, o ministério ainda não autorizou concursos para contratar docentes. Uma petição pública já recolheu mais de 2.650 assinaturas.

observador.title: 1,9 milhões para salvar encosta do castelo de Alcácer
observador.description: Câmara de Alcácer do Sal, no distrito de Setúbal, vai avançar com a empreitada de estabilização da encosta sul do castelo, num investimento de 1,9 milhões de euros, para prevenir novos deslizamentos.

observador.title: Esquerda critica orçamento de Lisboa para 2027
observador.description: Investimento em habitação cai mais de 40% face a 2025, enquanto benefícios fiscais rondam os 100 milhões. Partidos prometem propostas de alteração.

observador.title: Detido por tentar matar ex-namorada e o companheiro dela
observador.description: O suspeito, de 23 anos, embateu na viatura onde seguiam a ex-namorada e o companheiro e tentou atropelá-los por duas vezes. A PJ deteve-o dois dias depois.

observador.title: STF suspende prazos por falha da Microsoft
observador.description: Presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal atendeu pedido da OAB. Prazos retomam segunda-feira após falha no Outlook e Teams afetar o judiciário brasileiro.

observador.title: Aterro de Sobrado: associação contra renovação de licença
observador.description: A Jornada Principal contrapõe à Recivalongo, que prevê renovar a licença a 1 de dezembro, exigindo publicação integral de relatórios e encerramento imediato do aterro em Valongo.

observador.title: DBRS confirma rating de Portugal em "A" elevado
observador.description: Agência destaca redução da dívida e crescimento acima do esperado. Miranda Sarmento diz que desde abril de 2024 Portugal teve cinco subidas de rating.

observador.title: Lisboa prevê contrair empréstimo de 292 milhões de euros
observador.description: Com o PRR encerrado, Lisboa recorre a financiamento bancário faseado até 2029 para obras em áreas críticas. Dívida total ficará em 550,9 ME, abaixo do limite legal.

observador.title: Prisão preventiva para agressor da avó em Santarém
observador.description: Homem é suspeito de ter "agredido, ameaçado e coagido a avó", num contexto de violência que terá começado em 2018. O suspeito ficou sujeito à proibição de contactos com a vítima e as testemunhas.

observador.title: Advogado de Torres Vedras suspenso pela Ordem após burla
observador.description: A Ordem dos Advogados aplicou dois anos de suspensão e multa de 4.700€ a advogado de Torres Vedras condenado a quatro anos de prisão por burla. Há pelo menos dez processos em investigação.

observador.title: Aqui ao lado, há um país mais exótico do que o nosso
observador.description: Uma greve que não é contra o governo, mas contra a oposição. Um humorista que entrevista um político e se arrepende. Um chefe de governo que recusa uma missa pelas vítimas de uma tragédia. É normal?

observador.title: A destruição do país em cuecas
observador.description: Desconfio que, nas nações do Norte, em que o clima agreste é regra, os finlandeses e os suecos não possuem as residências atulhadas de embalagens da Renova.

observador.title: Os paradoxos do anti-racismo
observador.description: Afirmar uma superioridade racial é, sempre, uma expressão racista, mesmo quando é afirmada com o intuito contrário.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump trifft Wladimir Putin und Xi Jinping kommende Woche in China
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident möchte in Shenzhen mit seinen Amtskollegen aus China und Russland vor allem über Atomwaffen sprechen, nicht jedoch über die Ukraine. Kanzler Friedrich Merz hat eine klare Botschaft an Donald Trump: »Bitte keine Überraschungen«.

spiegel.title: Nations League: Deutschland gewinnt in Serbien – Brajan Gruda trifft bei Debüt
spiegel.description: In Belgrad spielt Jürgen Klopps DFB-Team Serbien an die Wand, bis der Regen zu stark wird. Brajan Gruda dribbelt wie ein Großer. In der Nations League verdient sich Deutschland so ein Endspiel gegen die Niederlande.

spiegel.title: Papst Leo XIV.: Eine halbe Million Menschen feiert den Papstbesuch an seiner alten Wirkungsstätte in Peru
spiegel.description: An den Plänen für seine bislang längste Auslandsreise hat das Oberhaupt der katholischen Kirche trotz seiner Krebserkrankung festgehalten. Bei der Rückkehr in seine frühere Diözese spricht der Papst von einem »Moment der Prüfung«.

spiegel.title: DFB-Einzelkritik gegen Serbien: Brajan Gruda beeindruckt beim Debüt, Florian Wirtz erfüllt die Führungsrolle
spiegel.description: In Serbien dominierte Deutschland einen schwachen Gegner. Da fiel niemand negativ auf – dafür aber positiv, allen voran der Neuling Brajan Gruda. So langsam tut sich eine Stammelf hervor.

spiegel.title: Nations League: Drei Erkenntnisse zu Deutschlands Sieg in Serbien
spiegel.description: Im zweiten Sieg unter Jürgen Klopp überzeugte vor allem Debütant Brajan Gruda. Der Bundestrainer scheint einen größeren Teil seiner ersten Elf gefunden zu haben. Das Spiel im Minutenprotokoll.

spiegel.title: Jesús de Miguel: Zwölf Spiele Sperre für Torwart Owono nach Todesfall in Spanien
spiegel.description: Nach einem harten Foul von Torhüter Jesús Owono erlitt Fußballprofi Jesús de Miguel einen Herzstillstand und starb wenig später. Nun gab der spanische Verband das Strafmaß gegen Owono bekannt.

spiegel.title: USA: Luftfahrtaufsicht verhängt landesweiten Flugstopp
spiegel.description: Für alle Flughäfen in den USA gilt derzeit ein Startverbot, dies hat die Luftfahrtaufsicht FAA entschieden. Grund ist offenbar eine Kommunikationsstörung.

spiegel.title: New Orleans: Tanker kollidiert mit Raddampfer – Passagiere und Crew in Sicherheit
spiegel.description: Nahe dem Hafen der US-Stadt New Orleans ist ein Tanker mit einem Schaufelradschiff zusammengestoßen. An Bord des Ausflugsschiffes befanden sich mehr als 130 Menschen. Offenbar wurden alle gerettet.

spiegel.title: Norwegen, Schweden und Estland sperren russische Sportler aus
spiegel.description: Das IOC und mehrere Dachverbände wollen Athletinnen und Athleten aus Russland wieder bei internationalen Wettkämpfen zulassen. Nun wehren sich immer mehr Länder mit verschärften Einreisebestimmungen.

spiegel.title: Sylvie Meis über »Die Friesenjunkies«: »Alle Genitalien waren abgeklebt und auch beim Masturbieren bewegt sich nur meine Schulter«
spiegel.description: Moderatorin Sylvie Meis stieß spontan zum Cast der Serie »Die Friesenjunkies«. Hier erklärt sie, warum ihr die Sexszenen leichter fielen als jene mit Drogen.

spiegel.title: Krieg in der Ukraine: Europäer einigen sich auf Verhandlungsteam für Gespräche mit Russland
spiegel.description: Deutschland, Frankreich, Großbritannien, Italien und Polen sollen gemeinsam mit den EU-Institutionen die Europäer bei Ukrainegesprächen mit Russland vertreten. Darauf haben sich die Staats- und Regierungschefs der EU-Staaten verständigt.

spiegel.title: Aachen: Mann auf offener Straße erschossen – Polizei fahndet nach Tatverdächtigen
spiegel.description: Im Aachener Ostviertel ist am Nachmittag ein 41-jähriger Mann getötet worden. Schon in der Nacht zuvor waren in der Umgebung Schüsse gefallen.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Experte schätzt 500.000 bis 600.000 Kriegstote auf russischer Seite
spiegel.description: Hacker haben viele Millionen Datensätze der russischen Behörde Rosstat erbeutet, darunter die geheime Todesstatistik. Der Russlandexperte Janis Kluge erklärt, warum das Leck so bedeutungsvoll ist – und was noch darin stecken könnte.

spiegel.title: Russland: Menschenrechtsanwältin Marija Bonzler zu langer Haft verurteilt

phys-org.title: Fiji petrel eludes 10-day search as communities aim to protect bird's habitat
phys-org.description: A new study details scientists' search for one of the planet's rarest birds in the waters off Fiji's Gau Island. Spanning 10 days, the expedition yielded no verified sightings of the critically endangered Fiji petrel, one of the world's most elusive birds. Fewer than 50 individuals are believed to remain on Earth.

phys-org.title: Unstable plasma heats itself with waves it generates, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: Fusion power is expected to be a sustainable energy source that emits no carbon dioxide during electricity generation. To achieve this, research is underway worldwide to confine high-temperature plasma using magnetic fields. To initiate a fusion reaction, high-energy particles or waves must be injected from outside to heat the plasma to extremely high temperatures.

phys-org.title: Same farms, different answers: When nitrogen pollution estimates don't add up
phys-org.description: To reduce nitrogen pollution stemming from synthetic fertilizer and livestock waste, California's Central Valley relies on five data sets to estimate surplus nitrogen. However, most parts of the United States use just one or two data sets—the U.S. Department of Agriculture's agricultural survey and census—to estimate nitrogen surplus.

phys-org.title: Hidden 'master switch' allows bacteria to breach the body's defenses
phys-org.description: Researchers at Penn Dental Medicine have uncovered a previously unknown molecular mechanism by which bacteria rapidly compromise the body's protective barriers, a finding that could reshape how scientists approach a wide range of serious diseases.

phys-org.title: 'Planimal' cells retain nearly entire algal genome after experimental cell fusion
phys-org.description: Most DNA in an organism is inherited from its parent or parents. This form of genetic inheritance is referred to as vertical inheritance because genes are passed down from generation to generation.

phys-org.title: Modified $450 3D printer builds living materials with more than 100 layers
phys-org.description: Living materials created with a 3D printer are like living tissues with one notable exception: You get to choose exactly which cells are in them, as well as their final 3D shape. Depending on the type of bacteria included in the print, the material can clean up contaminated water or break down waste materials such as plastic.

phys-org.title: Genomic analysis restores species status to 12 overlooked Great Barrier Reef corals
phys-org.description: An international team of scientists working with Queensland Museum's CoralBank project has uncovered previously hidden coral diversity on Australia's east coast, revealing that 12 corals once considered variations of other species are distinct species in their own right.

phys-org.title: Common ADHD classroom accommodations may not help students succeed, study finds
phys-org.description: Extra time on assignments. Frequent breaks. A quiet place to work. For students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), these are some of the most common accommodations schools provide to make learning easier. But are they actually helping children succeed? A new study from Florida International University (FIU) suggests that some widely used approaches may be falling short.

phys-org.title: Happy face, angry voice: Human–dog interaction study tracks conflicting cues
phys-org.description: Dogs, having lived alongside humans for tens of thousands of years, are keenly tuned in to our emotions. Behavioral experiments, brain studies and even measurements of heart rate all suggest dogs respond differently depending on the emotional expressions they encounter in humans.

phys-org.title: A perfect couple: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis
phys-org.description: They say opposites attract, and many couples do fit this pattern. One is pragmatic and down-to-earth, while the other is a dreamer with their head in the clouds. Yet, these differences make them perfect for each other. According to researchers at ICFO, chemical interactions between atoms are not that different. phys-org.title: A newly discovered South African dinosaur was a heavyweight even as a youngster
phys-org.description: It probably walked on two legs and weighed about 400 kilograms (880 pounds), despite still being a youngster. Meet Nyana rooiwalensis, a newly identified dinosaur species that lived more than 200 million years ago in what is now South Africa.

phys-org.title: Molecular sensor makes invisible traces of mercury easier to see
phys-org.description: Mercury contamination presents an obvious challenge: it is invisible. A glass of water or a piece of fruit can seem perfectly normal to the naked eye, even when trace amounts of toxic mercury are present. Detecting such minute levels usually requires specialized laboratory tools and trained experts.

phys-org.title: Fruit fly sleep protein yields peptides that inhibit drug-resistant bacteria in lab tests
phys-org.description: Researchers at University of Tsukuba and collaborating institutions have identified short antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri, a sleep-inducing protein in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. The research is published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: New genetic atlas reveals traces of 10,000 years of sheep breeding
phys-org.description: For around 10,000 years, humans have selectively bred sheep for desirable traits. Generation after generation, we have chosen animals for their wool, size and reproductive characteristics and gradually left our mark on their DNA.

phys-org.title: Ancient rocks reveal a dramatic journey from deep inside Earth
phys-org.description: Surface rocks can reveal records of regions they occupied millions of years ago, even if those areas were kilometers below ground. On Türkiye's Marmara Sea's southern shores and islands, granitic rocks that are now exposed originated as molten material deep in Earth's crust.

phys-org.title: Evolution found another way to build a primate brain
phys-org.description: What makes the human brain so much larger and more complex than the brains of many other mammals? Scientists have long sought clues in our DNA. Some discoveries show how genetic changes enable the developing brain to produce more cells. Others help explain how long those cells can continue to multiply.

phys-org.title: Mountain growth spurts may have sparked complex life on Earth
phys-org.description: Mountain ranges grew higher throughout Earth's history in two distinct "spurts" that correlated with the flourishing of biological diversity on our planet, according to new research published in the journal Science Advances. The study suggests mountains may have played a key role in sparking complex life.

phys-org.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
phys-org.description: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star.

undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: The Rare-Earth Game
proj-syn.description: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

proj-syn.title: Why Research Matters
proj-syn.description: Over the past 21 months, in the country that has leveraged research to greatest effect, the government is slashing funding for it, closing centers where it is done, politicizing grant-making decisions, and bullying its single biggest engine: universities. The costs will be far greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Africa Needs a Different Kind of Climate Finance
proj-syn.description: Roughly half of the climate finance that flows to Africa comes in the form of debt, with multilateral and bilateral development-finance institutions often lending at commercial rates to economies already struggling to carry the added costs. To maximize fiscal space, the instruments used to deliver climate finance need to change.

proj-syn.title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
proj-syn.description: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
proj-syn.description: How Mexico’s left has managed to retain strong support is a key question of contemporary Latin American politics. The most likely answer centers on the ruling Morena party’s pragmatic brand of left-wing politics, which combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.

proj-syn.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
proj-syn.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.

proj-syn.title: The ASEAN Paradox
proj-syn.description: As the Association of Southeast Asian Nations gathers for its 49th Summit, several rifts have exposed the group’s institutional shortcomings. But amid a fracturing global order, ASEAN must choose: turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.

proj-syn.title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
proj-syn.description: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome. A comfort-by-design approach could overcome these obstacles by involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring that new systems work with existing medical practices.

proj-syn.title: Reviving the Legacy of Reykjavík
proj-syn.description: As nuclear threats grow, AI accelerates, and international law comes under strain, the world urgently needs a renewed commitment to dialogue. Today's leaders can find a template in the landmark 1986 summit between then US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dreams Exceed Its Grid
proj-syn.description: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

proj-syn.title: What the US Midterms Could Mean for AI
proj-syn.description: Now that the Democrats will hold sizable majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, they have an opening to push for long-overdue legislation to steer AI development toward the common good. Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Publish AI-Generated Articles!
proj-syn.description: Peer-reviewed academic journals exist to advance our knowledge and understanding by publishing the best work being done in a given field. If that is the goal, and the best reviewers—both human and AI—agree that an article generated by AI meets that standard, why should a journal's editors reject it?

proj-syn.title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
proj-syn.description: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional. With voters across the United States rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opportunity to enact meaningful regulation and hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: It’s the Corruption, Stupid
proj-syn.description: Fed up with Donald Trump and his family's blatant profiteering, Americans dealt Republicans a resounding defeat in this month’s midterm elections. Democrats won by linking corruption to the cost-of-living crisis, but the party’s establishment remains compromised and must clean house before 2028.

proj-syn.title: The Fed's Risky Retreat From Transparency
proj-syn.description: Kevin Warsh, the new chair of the US Federal Reserve, is not wrong to abandon the practice of forward guidance. But if he continues to withhold information about how the central bank intends to assess the economic outlook and determine the appropriate stance of monetary policy, he is in for a rude awakening.

proj-syn.title: An Owl’s Guide to US-China Coexistence
proj-syn.description: In 2027 and beyond, the United States should lay the foundation for a stable coexistence with China, not a contest to “win.” A clear-eyed approach is needed to help make “the world safe for diversity,” as John F. Kennedy put it in 1963.

proj-syn.title: AI Investors Have Overlooked Obvious Risks
proj-syn.description: Prior to the US midterm elections on November 3, financial markets had been treating generative AI as some kind of unstoppable force that could not be hampered by higher interest rates or political and social resistance. But now reality may be setting in.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Over the past few decades, we have adopted a new framework for thinking about privacy that centers our experience in the digital realm, conflates privacy with secrecy, and fails to account for the insecurity surveillance generates. As a result, even privacy advocates often undermine their own cause.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Nvidia’s Startup Funding Deals Hit A Record. What’s Next After Huang?
crunchbase.description: Before it was thrust into crisis this week, Nvidia was steadily continuing its pace as one of the busiest startup investors around, including backing many of the biggest venture deals of 2026. We take a fresh look at where Nvidia and its venture arm NVentures have been investing and what the future could hold.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Agentic AI And Infrastructure Are Still On A Roll

crunchbase.title: Protein Startups Are Selling Lots Of Snacks And Drinks. Our Sample Tasting Found Most Neither Great Nor Horrible
crunchbase.description: As we chronicled earlier this week, both startups and established food brands are making it simpler than ever to up protein intake. From sodas to snack bars to ice cream, it’s now possible to get a fix of this coveted macronutrient with foods and drinks more commonly associated with sugar, starch and fat. But, do they taste good? To find out, we hit up a local Target for a selection of protein foods sold by venture-backed startups and subjected them to a taste test. Here are our findings.

crunchbase.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
crunchbase.description: Founders should treat dependence on app stores as infrastructure risk, since a sudden removal can disrupt customer access, subscriptions and revenue with no reliable path to reinstatement. Sharing his experience, Yakov Filippenko, founder and CEO of Intch, suggests that building and testing alternative access and payment channels before a crisis can help keep the business operating.

crunchbase.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
crunchbase.description: Recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. We take a look.

On Tuesday, the AI giant submitted an updated S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering, unveiling new details including a proposed share price range offering size.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old
crunchbase.description: A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The board also reached a new record of 1,900 private companies last month, along with a new record for the U.S. with more than 1,000 private unicorn companies.

crunchbase.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
crunchbase.description: AI can help startups reduce patent preparation costs, but DIY applications may overlook critical issues. In this guest commentary, attorneys Michael Drapkin and Nathan Mutter of AI-Native law firm Landfall IP, argue that combining AI with legal expertise can produce more efficient, commercially valuable patent protection that withstands investor scrutiny and is harder for competitors to circumvent.
